name: control-room
description: A big-button control panel for driving Claude Code from inside the editor.

commands.title: Control Room: Open every control room in this workspace
Control Room: Resume a Claude session in a terminal
Control Room: Install the session-start watch hook
Control Room: Close the Claude tab (clears a stale session it keeps reopening)

controlRoom.logPath.description: Where chat.jsonl lives. Empty means every control-room* folder in the workspace is offered as a separate panel; setting it pins the extension to one log.

controlRoom.openOnStartup.description: Open the Control Room panel when the workspace opens, so no palette step is needed. With several control rooms in the workspace the primary one opens; switching happens inside the panel.

controlRoom.mirrorEditorChat.description: Copy the Claude tab's conversation into the panel, so it holds both sides rather than only what was typed in it. Mirrored lines are marked and are never answered a second time.

enumDescriptions: No terminal at all: the session runs as a background Claude session (claude --bg), and claude attach reaches it if you want to look.
Every terminal this extension opens becomes an editor tab.
The terminal view at the bottom, as before.
controlRoom.startTerminal.markdownDescription: How this extension starts a Claude session. `hidden` (the default) starts it as a BACKGROUND session with `claude --bg` — there is no terminal to hide, and `claude attach <id>` opens it if you want to watch; the panel offers that when a session does not answer. `tab` runs it in an editor tab, `panel` in the terminal view at the bottom. A background start that fails falls back to a tab, with the reason printed in the room.

controlRoom.autoTrust.description: When VS Code trusts the workspace, record the same trust for Claude Code, so a session started in a hidden terminal is not stopped by "Do you trust the files in this folder?".

controlRoom.claudeWindowHandoff.markdownDescription: Let the Claude window open a conversation this room is running in the background. Control Room installs a small wrapper as `claudeCode.claudeProcessWrapper` that releases the conversation from the room just before the window resumes it — without it the window fails with "Claude Code process exited with code 1". Turning this off removes the wrapper setting (only if it is Control Room's own); a wrapper you set yourself is never replaced.
